name: Otto von Bismarck
roles: Federal Chancellor of the German Empire

life_arc.notes: Born into Prussian landed nobility; studied law; entered Prussian politics and developed a strongly conservative, monarchist worldview.
Served in the Prussian Landtag and diplomatic posts. His diplomacy in Frankfurt, St Petersburg and Paris broadened his understanding of European power politics.
Appointed Prussian Minister-President in 1862. Used military reform, diplomacy, limited wars and coalition management to strengthen Prussia and achieve German unification.
As Chancellor, shifted from expansion to preservation: alliance management, isolation of France, conservative domestic policy, economic/social reforms and crisis prevention.
Dismissed by Kaiser Wilhelm II in 1890 after strategic and personal conflict. Spent retirement writing memoirs and influencing public memory of his statecraft.

typical_failure_modes: overconfidence in personal control of the system
managing complexity through elite bargains rather than broad legitimacy
core_principles_reconstructed: Treat power relationships as constraints before pursuing ideals.
Use limited objectives and preserve an exit route.
Avoid fighting multiple major opponents simultaneously.
After a strategic victory, consolidate rather than automatically seek another victory.

sources: Otto von Bismarck, Gedanken und Erinnerungen (Memoirs)
Lothar Gall, Bismarck: The White Revolutionary
